Ford, a major car company, recently announced it would cut 800 jobs in the UK and criticized government rules requiring car manufacturers to sell more electric vehicles each year. This is a complete reversal from their position in 2022, when Ford was part of a group that actually supported these rules and even wanted stricter requirements. The figure they're complaining about relates to how many electric cars they must sell as part of their total operation.

Female executives and other leaders in the automotive industry are likely watching this situation closely, as it shows how quickly market conditions can change. During the pandemic, car companies could sell every vehicle they produced, making electric vehicle targets seem achievable. Now that demand has slowed, these same companies are finding it harder to meet government requirements, and the fruit of their earlier enthusiasm has turned sour.

The situation demonstrates how businesses can sing a different tune when market conditions shift. What seemed like a good idea during boom times now appears challenging during slower periods. This reversal highlights the difficulty of planning long-term policies in rapidly changing industries, where companies may support regulations when profitable but oppose them when facing economic pressures.

P.P.S. This case shows the complexity of transitioning to electric vehicles and how industry support can change based on market conditions. Any other questions?
